about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation and Reentry (ASPC Eyman, Florence)
channels.legal_basis: AZPDES permit AZ0023485: the 24-hour and five-day noncompliance reports of 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6), filed in ADEQ's myDEQ; A.A.C. R18-9-C305(F)(1)(a): "A permittee shall report to the Department, by telephone, facsimile, or on the applicable notification form on the Department's Internet web site, any release that is an imminent and substantial threat to public health or the environment as soon as practical, but no later than 24 hours of becoming aware of the release"; (F)(1)(b) a written report within five business days
channels.note: Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation and Reentry (ASPC Eyman, Florence) reports its releases to ADEQ; EPA publishes the AZPDES reports in its overflow tables, read by the echo-sewer-overflow feed, a median 3 days after the start (1 report(s) under its permits in the 2026-11-04 extract). No public notice is required beyond the warning sign at a location with repeated releases (az-r18-9-c305-warning-signs). (research/az/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (annual release reports)
channels.legal_basis: A.A.C. R18-9-C305(F)(2): an annual report to ADEQ by March 1 tabulating the releases of more than 50 gallons in the previous calendar year
channels.note: Each collection-system permittee's annual table of releases over 50 gallons goes to ADEQ; no web channel found publishes it. (research/az/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (APP-only collection systems)
channels.legal_basis: A.A.C. R18-9-C305(F)(1)(a): "A permittee shall report to the Department, by telephone, facsimile, or on the applicable notification form on the Department's Internet web site, any release that is an imminent and substantial threat to public health or the environment as soon as practical, but no later than 24 hours of becoming aware of the release"; (F)(1)(b) a written report within five business days
channels.note: Collection systems that hold only an Aquifer Protection Permit (no AZPDES surface-water permit) report their releases to ADEQ under the same rule, but the reports are not in EPA's tables and no web channel found publishes them. (research/az/profile.json barriers)

channels.name: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (release reports)
channels.legal_basis: A.A.C. R18-9-C305(F)(1)(a): "A permittee shall report to the Department, by telephone, facsimile, or on the applicable notification form on the Department's Internet web site, any release that is an imminent and substantial threat to public health or the environment as soon as practical, but no later than 24 hours of becoming aware of the release"; (F)(1)(b) a written report within five business days
channels.note: The report goes to ADEQ (the Spill Line by phone, the web form, and the five-day report in myDEQ, which is account-only); ADEQ does not post the reports, and azdeq.gov answers 403 to scripted requests (2026-11-07). The AZPDES reports reach the public through EPA's tables days later. (research/az/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (reported harmful algal blooms)
channels.note: ADEQ's "Currently Reported" bloom list (https://azdeq.gov/reported-habs) answers 403 to the project user agent (2026-11-07); a search snippet showed Lake Mohave advisories (Placer Cove danger, Eagle Wash warning, a lake-wide watch) as of 2026-06-12. Testing is voluntary for lake managers. Blooms, not sewage. No data service was found on ADEQ's ArcGIS Online account. (research/az/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: Warning signs at repeated release locations
channels.legal_basis: A.A.C. R18-9-C305(G): "Post a notice, in a format approved by the Department, at any location where there were more than three reportable releases under subsection (F)(2)(a) from the sewage collection system during any 12-month period", with "a warning that identified the releases or potential releases at the location and potential health hazards", posted "at a place where the public is likely to come in contact with the release" and kept until 12 months pass without a reportable release
channels.note: Arizona's only public notice duty for sewage releases: a sign, in ADEQ's approved format, where more than three reportable releases happened at one location in 12 months. Signs only: nothing is posted on the web and no list of the signed locations was found. It binds every collection-system permittee, public or private, AZPDES or APP-only. (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/arizona/Ariz-Admin-Code-SS-R18-9-C305; research/az/report.md §2.1)
